lede: Victorians vote today, with the final Newspoll putting Jess Wilson's Coalition on 33% and Labor on just 20%, ahead of One Nation and the Greens.
The US disabled another ship trying to run its blockade of Iranian ports, while Houthi strikes on Saudi refineries helped push Brent crude to US$96.57.
The ASX 200 rose 0.8% on Friday to 8,833.6, capping its best week since August as copper and gold miners rallied.

stories.h: US disables another ship trying to break its Iran blockade
stories.b: US Central Command says aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau flagged bulk carrier Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday, knocking out its engines after it ignored warnings on leaving Bandar Abbas. No crew were hurt. It is at least the 15th ship the US has disabled since the blockade began in spring. CENTCOM says 158 ships have been turned around and six disabled since the blockade resumed in July.
stories.w: Each clash at sea adds risk to Gulf shipping, which flows through to oil prices and Australian petrol bowsers.

stories.h: Saudi Arabia's allies condemn Houthi strikes on its oil refineries
stories.b: Ministers from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey met in Islamabad under their August defence pact, which treats an attack on one as an attack on all, and condemned Houthi attacks on the kingdom. The Houthis claimed a strike on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery, on Wednesday, and a projectile hit a refinery in Jazan on Thursday, killing a worker. No new concrete measures were announced.
stories.w: Attacks on Saudi oil sites on top of the Hormuz crisis squeeze a second big supply source, which is why Brent jumped this week.

stories.h: Spain's campaign ends with the two big parties nearly level
stories.b: Campaigning wrapped up on Friday before Sunday's snap election, with one late poll showing Pedro Sánchez's Socialists and Alberto Núñez Feijóo's People's Party almost tied. Private polls still give the People's Party and the far right Vox a combined majority, while the state pollster has the Socialists first. Housing costs are voters' top worry.
stories.w: A win for the right would move another big EU economy away from the centre left, with Vox likely holding the balance.

quick.x: Israel's coalition parties reportedly agreed key principles of a law on drafting ultra Orthodox men into the army, a long running fight in Israeli politics.
Satellite images show Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites as Riyadh steps up its own attacks on Yemen.

stories.h: Nvidia pauses AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
stories.b: Nvidia has reportedly told partners including Dell and Super Micro to halt AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. It follows a new US Commerce Department rule requiring licences for advanced AI chips going to data centres in those countries and Brazil. The aim is to stop Chinese firms renting restricted computing power from offshore data centres.
stories.w: Southeast Asia has been a data centre boom zone, and tighter US controls could redirect investment, possibly toward places like Australia.

stories.h: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler for about US$43.9 billion
stories.b: Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike will buy rival Zscaler in an all stock deal, giving Zscaler holders 1.135 CrowdStrike shares each, about a 34% premium. CrowdStrike shareholders would own about 84% of the combined company, which would start with more than US$10 billion in annual recurring revenue. It still needs Zscaler shareholder approval.
stories.w: It is one of the biggest cybersecurity mergers ever, and shows security buyers want fewer, bigger platforms rather than lots of separate tools.

stories.h: Amazon and other sites push back on AI shopping agents
stories.b: AI agents from OpenAI, Meta, Google and others that browse and buy on a user's behalf are running into blocks from Amazon and a growing number of retailers over Black Friday. Amazon has changed its site code to shut out outside agents while promoting its own assistant, Rufus. Retailers worry about losing control of pricing, customer data and the shopping experience.
stories.w: Who controls the checkout in an AI world is shaping up as the next big fight between tech platforms and retailers.

quick.x: The ACCC told shoppers to set spending limits and check permissions before letting AI agents buy for them, and said consumer law rights still apply.
Singapore officials say they are talking to local firms to assess the impact of Nvidia's shipment pause.

stories.h: Victorians vote today with Labor facing a historic swing
stories.b: Polls close at 6pm across all 88 lower house seats and 40 upper house seats. The final Newspoll had the Coalition on 33%, Labor 20%, One Nation 18% and the Greens 17%, with Jess Wilson leading Premier Ben Carroll 51 to 34 as preferred premier. Analysts say Labor faces its biggest swing in more than 70 years.
stories.w: A change of government would end 12 years of Labor rule in Victoria and test how far One Nation's surge turns into seats.

stories.h: Albanese rules out a reshuffle as the political year ends
stories.b: At his end of year press conference, the PM said there would be no cabinet reshuffle for now, backed Jim Chalmers and Chris Bowen, and promised a big agenda for next year. He conceded the government does not get everything right. His net approval sits at a record low of minus 31 in Newspoll, with Labor and One Nation tied on 27%.
stories.w: With Labor's vote at historic lows, summer is when pressure on the leadership and the ministry usually builds.

stories.h: Labor shifts into election mode at the halfway mark
stories.b: Michelle Grattan writes that Labor's national campaign committee met this week as the government passes the midpoint of its term. There has been speculation about whether Albanese might hand over before the next election, which he has rejected. Parliament has now risen for the year.
stories.w: The early campaign footing signals Labor sees One Nation and a weak economy as serious threats.

quick.x: One Nation texted Victorians on polling day urging them to oppose a Coalition plan to privatise sewerage services.
Final Victorian polls showed One Nation slipping to between 16% and 18%, though the Coalition still looks set for a big win.

stories.h: ASX caps its best week since August
stories.b: The ASX 200 rose 0.8% on Friday to close at 8,833.6, up 2.8% for the week. WiseTech jumped about 15%, copper miners rallied on a surge in copper futures and gold was up nearly 2%. Wall Street was closed for Thanksgiving.
stories.w: The bounce comes despite hot inflation data this week, suggesting investors think the worst of the AI sell off has passed for now.

stories.h: Steadfast holders back the $6 a share buyout
stories.b: Shareholders in insurance broker Steadfast voted 99.58% in favour of the takeover by KKR and Dragoneer. The court hearing is set for 22 December, shares should stop trading on 23 December and the deal is due to complete on 19 January. Regulatory clearances are still outstanding.
stories.w: Another big ASX company is heading into private equity hands, shrinking the pool of listed stocks for super funds and retail investors.

stories.h: ASIC tests Morgans over conflicts in the failed Firmus float
stories.b: ASIC chair Sarah Court told a parliamentary committee the regulator has met broker Morgans to test potential conflicts of interest over AI data centre firm Firmus's withdrawn listing. Morgans staff and clients reportedly invested $560 million in Firmus before the float without disclosing it. Court said the inquiries have not become an enforcement investigation.
stories.w: How ASIC handles this will shape trust in big ASX floats after one of the largest planned listings collapsed in October.

quick.x: The ACCC is running another check on retail sale claims over Black Friday and Cyber Monday and warned about AI made fake stores and deepfake ads.
Spot gold rose about 1.8% to US$3,634.90 an ounce on Friday, while iron ore held near US$90.70 a tonne, and nine of 11 ASX sectors finished higher.
Firmus pulled its float in October after failing to win enough support at $11 a share and will now seek private capital.

explainer.body: In an all stock takeover, the buyer pays with its own shares instead of cash. Target shareholders get a fixed number of buyer shares for each share they own, called the exchange ratio, like the 1.135 CrowdStrike shares offered per Zscaler share. That means the deal's dollar value moves with the buyer's share price until it closes. The upside is the buyer does not need to borrow, and target holders keep a stake in the combined company; the downside is existing buyer shareholders get diluted.

ahead.e: Victorian election: polls close 6pm, counting tonight.
Spain holds its snap national election; OPEC+ meets on output.
ABS releases September quarter GDP; Jensen Huang briefs US House committees (Tue 1 Dec US time).
Jensen Huang testifies at a US Senate hearing on export controls (Thu 3 Dec US time).
US government funding runs out (11 Dec US time), with the Iran war at the centre of the fight.
